I don't have the day's price move for MPC, so I can't tell you whether the stock went up or down today. However, the refining environment shown in your data suggests crosscurrents: US crude is at $99.64 per barrel while refineries are running at a healthy 94.5 percent capacity, but Brent crude (the global benchmark) dipped below $90 on hopes that the Iran conflict might ease—a development that could weigh on margins if sustained, since lower oil prices compress what refiners earn per gallon processed.

The news does show real tension. President Trump signaled the Iran situation could end "fairly soon," which spooked oil markets lower, but his own Secretary of State Rubio said diplomatic talks remain stalled with "outrageous" Iranian demands. That gap between the President's optimism and his negotiator's reality suggests the market may not fully believe a quick resolution yet—which is why oil hasn't collapsed further. For Marathon specifically, any sustained drop in crude prices would eventually hurt profitability, even at high utilization rates.
